source: RFC 0007 §7.4.7 (control-typed-api decisions of 2026-11-21: writer model B, the role class cosec:manage-roles)
statement: The role class: a change of a tenant's document that only writes or removes roles (putRole, removeRole), by an author who holds cosec:manage-roles on that document, needs no second person on account of who grants, unless one of those roles has no app or is of the control plane's own app (cosec.control.app-id), the role written or the one the head holds under its id, which a putRole replaces and so removes: putting or removing such a role is analyzed as before and waits for a person, since a member of it holds control calls on its tenant's document, governors of the control plane being for a person to appoint. The exclusion is keyed on the role's app, not on its actions' names, and that is enough: a binding a tenant's role derives is scoped to its app, and a control request is decided in the control app, so a role of any other app permits no control call whatever its catalog's actions say. It sees every escalation of the change, the grant analysis's and the others' (a break-glass binding's), and lifts only when every one is one it may lift, each safe for a holder: CROSS_TENANT is a service principal's case, a principal outside the tenant projecting its roles; NOT_COVERED arises for a holder inside the tenant handing out catalog permissions it does not itself hold, which is what managing roles means; DENY_OVERLAP arises when a DENY that binds the author may overlap what the role grants, and a DENY still binds whomever it binds at decision time (deny-first), so lifting the overlap grants nothing a DENY forbids. It records one informational ROLE_CLASS escalation in their place, naming the holder and what it lifted; anything the analysis could not tell (an unreadable app document, an unresolved policy, a spent budget) still waits. cosec:write on each role and cosec:grant on each binding a role derives are decided as before; a change that writes anything else is analyzed whole; an app's or the platform's document is never the class's. The grant is decided again at publish, as the publisher, on the current heads, as the whole grant analysis is: a grant withdrawn after the check, while the change is checked, shadowing or ready, sends it back to AWAITING_APPROVAL, and nothing publishes. A check answers the same: a holder learns the change will not wait, anyone else the escalation it would wait on. Its bounds are the format's: a tenant's document holds no "*" role and the platform's none at all; a tenant's role derives only bindings of its own tenant's members, in its app, to the permission policies that app's document defines (a tenant cannot write a perm: policy, and a permission its app does not define does not publish); a member reaches nothing outside its own tenant's document, whatever the app's catalog grants (TenantIsolation); the tenant's boundary caps what such a role permits.
